::: {#def-bh}
#### Benjamini--Hochberg procedure

Given the cutoff rank $\hat k$ of @def-bh-cutoff,
the **Benjamini--Hochberg procedure** (BH) rejects $H_{(1)}, \ldots, H_{(\hat k)}$ and no others.

Source: Benjamini and Hochberg [-@benjamini1995controlling].

Source: @wikipedia_false_discovery_rate.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#rem-bh-step-up}
#### BH is a step-up procedure

Holm's procedure starts at the smallest p-value and stops at the first failure.
BH starts at the largest p-value and works down until one passes its threshold $k q / m$.
Every hypothesis ranked at or below $\hat k$ is rejected,
including those with p-values above their own thresholds.
The thresholds $k q / m$ grow with the rank $k$,
and the smallest, $q / m$, equals the Bonferroni threshold,
so BH rejects every hypothesis that the Bonferroni correction rejects at level $\siglevel = q$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: {#exm-bh}
#### The BH procedure for the Khan genes

```{r}
#| label: bh-reject
#| code-fold: false
bh_reject <- function(p, q) {
  m <- length(p)
  ord <- order(p)
  passes <- which(p[ord] <= seq_len(m) * q / m)
  k_hat <- if (length(passes) > 0) max(passes) else 0
  reject <- rep(FALSE, m)
  reject[ord[seq_len(k_hat)]] <- TRUE
  reject
}
```

For the first ten genes at $q = 0.05$ the thresholds $k \times 0.05 / 10$ rise from $0.005$ to $0.05$:

```{r}
#| label: bh-ten-genes
bh_ten <- data.frame(
  gene = names(ten_genes),
  p_value = ten_genes,
  row.names = NULL
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(p_value) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    rank = dplyr::row_number(),
    threshold = rank * alpha / length(ten_genes),
    passes = p_value <= threshold
  )
bh_ten |>
  dplyr::mutate(p_value = fmt_p(p_value)) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The largest rank that passes is $\hat k =$ `r max(which(bh_ten$passes))`,
so BH rejects the `r max(which(bh_ten$passes))` genes with the smallest p-values.
On all 2308 genes at $q = 0.05$, BH rejects far more genes than the Bonferroni correction:

```{r}
#| label: bh-khan
#| code-fold: false
c(
  unadjusted = sum(khan_p <= 0.05),
  bonferroni = sum(bonferroni_reject(khan_p, 0.05)),
  holm = sum(holm_reject(khan_p, 0.05)),
  bh = sum(bh_reject(khan_p, 0.05))
)
```

A guarantee that $\text{FDR} \le 0.05$ is a statement about the average false discovery proportion over repeated data sets,
not about this particular list of `r sum(bh_reject(khan_p, 0.05))` genes.
:::
